react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolome is driven by a coordinated perturbation of methionine metabolism and its connected one-carbon/folate pool. Across three independent enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA (Reactome + SMPDB + KEGG + WikiPathways), mummichog m/z-network activity, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA — the KEGG 'Methionine Metabolism' map (hsa00670) emerges as the top cross-paradigm winner (MetaboAnalystR rank 1, p=3.36e-07; RaMP rank 4, FDR 1.19e-13; mummichog rank 2, p=0.0155), with 5 input metabolites — L-methionine (KEGG:C00073), S-adenosylmethionine (KEGG:C00019), homocysteine (KEGG:C00155), choline (KEGG:C00114), and adenosine (KEGG:C00212) — hitting the pathway. The driver metabolites define the canonical cycle: L-methionine is the entry substrate converted by methionine adenosyltransferase to SAM, which donates its methyl group to methyltransferases and generates SAH that is hydrolyzed to adenosine and homocysteine; homocysteine is then either remethylated (requiring folate/betaine) or enters the transsulfuration branch. Choline feeds the betaine-dependent remethylation route. Cysteic acid (C00506) maps to the downstream cysteine-oxidation arm of transsulfuration, confirming full flux through the cycle. Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:map00260) ranks as a secondary consensus hit (RaMP rank 0, FDR 3.75e-19) via shared one-carbon donors (L-threonine, L-glutamic acid, choline), consistent with a broad perturbation of one-carbon metabolism affecting both methionine and glycine cycles simultaneously. The lipid signals (15-HETE, 8-HPETE) point to secondary lipoxygenase activity on arachidonic acid, which does not reach significance in ORA and likely reflects inflammatory co-activation downstream of oxidative stress in the one-carbon pool.

react_result.final_narrative_text:
The differential metabolome is dominated by a coherent cluster of sulfur-amino-acid metabolites centred on the methionine–homocysteine–SAM axis, anchored by L-methionine (KEGG:C00073), L-homocysteine (KEGG:C00155), S-adenosyl-L-methionine (KEGG:C00019), and cysteic acid (KEGG:C00506). These four compounds constitute the strongest cross-paradigm signal: they are the driver hit-set in KEGG:hsa00670 (One Carbon Pool by Folate, p = 3.36 × 10⁻⁷ in MetaboAnalystR PSEA), the top-ranked Methionine Metabolism pathway in RaMP multi-DB ORA (KEGG:map00270, FDR = 1.19 × 10⁻¹³), and the methionine/cysteine module in mummichog (p = 0.016). Adenosine (KEGG:C00212) — the methyl-group donor that activates methionine to SAM — is also recorded as a hit in the RaMP methionine pathway, reinforcing the centrality of one-carbon methylation chemistry. A secondary cluster of compounds — L-threonine (KEGG:C00188), choline (KEGG:C00114), and L-glutamic acid (KEGG:C00025) — maps to Glycine, Serine and Threonine Metabolism (RaMP: KEGG:map00260, FDR = 3.75 × 10⁻¹⁹; MetaboAnalystR: hsa00260, p = 0.0204; mummichog: MUMM:glycine_serine_alanine_and_threonine_metabolism, p = 0.016). The methionine and serine/threonine clusters are biologically coupled: the folate one-carbon pool supplies methyl groups to homocysteine for re-methylation to methionine, and threonine catabolism feeds into homocysteine synthesis. Choline oxidation is a secondary source of methyl groups linking these pathways. A third signal — 15(S)-HETE (KEGG:C04742), 8(S)-HPETE (KEGG:C14823), and L-glutamic acid — appears in the mummichog network as arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism, p = 0.016), though it is absent from the ORA tools. Choline (KEGG:C00114) additionally hits glycerophospholipid metabolism in mummichog, consistent with its role as a precursor for phosphatidylcholine synthesis. The two primary pathways — methionine/one-carbon metabolism and glycine/serine/threonine metabolism — are the robust cross-paradigm winners, supported by three complementary methods and multiple database namespaces.

Limitations: FELLA random-walk diffusion failed at runtime and could not be used to capture indirect pathway neighbours. The arachidonic-acid signal was detected only by mummichog and should be interpreted with caution pending orthogonal validation.

  "narrative_text": "Cross-paradigm analysis of the 13 differentially abundant metabolites revealed convergent enrichment across three major metabolic themes. The most robust consensus emerged around methionine and cysteine metabolism: MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (hsa00670, raw p = 3.36e-07) and Mummichog m/z-direct analysis (Methionine and cysteine metabolism, p = 0.019) both identified the same four driver metabolites — S-adenosyl-L-methionine (KEGG:C00019), L-homocysteine (KEGG:C00155), L-methionine (KEGG:C00073), and L-cysteic acid (KEGG:C00506) — driving this pathway. The methionine cycle sits at the intersection of folate-mediated one-carbon metabolism and transsulfuration, linking S-adenosylmethionine-dependent methylation to homocysteine recycling and cysteine biosynthesis. A second cross-tool consensus appeared in glycine, serine and threonine metabolism: Mummichog ranked it first (p = 0.019) with L-threonine (KEGG:C00188), L-methionine (KEGG:C00073), choline (KEGG:C00114), and L-glutamic acid (KEGG:C00025) as hits, while RaMP ORA enriched KEGG:map00260 (FDR 1.28e-06) with L-threonine, (R)-lipoic acid (KEGG:C16241) and L-ornithine. A third axis appeared in lipid-mediated signalling: Mummichog identified arachidonic acid metabolism (p = 0.019) with 8(S)-HPETE (KEGG:C14823) and 15-HETE (KEGG:C04742) as hits, and glycerophospholipid metabolism (p = 0.070) with choline co-occurring alongside HETE species — consistent with phospholipase A2-mediated release of arachidonate from membrane lipids. react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm analysis of the 13 differentially abundant metabolites revealed convergent enrichment across three major metabolic themes. The most robust consensus emerged around methionine and cysteine metabolism: MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (hsa00670, raw p = 3.36e-07) and Mummichog m/z-direct analysis (Methionine and cysteine metabolism, p = 0.019) both identified the same four driver metabolites — S-adenosyl-L-methionine (KEGG:C00019), L-homocysteine (KEGG:C00155), L-methionine (KEGG:C00073), and L-cysteic acid (KEGG:C00506) — driving this pathway. The methionine cycle sits at the intersection of folate-mediated one-carbon metabolism and transsulfuration, linking S-adenosylmethionine-dependent methylation to homocysteine recycling and cysteine biosynthesis. A second cross-tool consensus appeared in glycine, serine and threonine metabolism: Mummichog ranked it first (p = 0.019) with L-threonine (KEGG:C00188), L-methionine (KEGG:C00073), choline (KEGG:C00114), and L-glutamic acid (KEGG:C00025) as hits, while RaMP ORA enriched KEGG:map00260 (FDR 1.28e-06) with L-threonine, (R)-lipoic acid (KEGG:C16241) and L-ornithine. A third axis appeared in lipid-mediated signalling: Mummichog identified arachidonic acid metabolism (p = 0.019) with 8(S)-HPETE (KEGG:C14823) and 15-HETE (KEGG:C04742) as hits, and glycerophospholipid metabolism (p = 0.070) with choline co-occurring alongside HETE species — consistent with phospholipase A2-mediated release of arachidonate from membrane lipids. Adenosine (KEGG:C00212) was recovered as a hit in methionine-and-cysteine metabolism under Mummichog and in hsa00670 under MetaboAnalystR, consistent with its role as a product of S-adenosylhomocysteine hydrolysis in the methylation cycle. Across all three paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KSEA, and Mummichog m/z-direct), methionine-and-cysteine metabolism was the sole pathway appearing in the top-five results of ≥ 2 tools with shared driver metabolites, making it the primary cross-paradigm winner.

  "narrative_text": "The differential metabolome is driven by a coordinated perturbation of methionine metabolism and its connected one-carbon/folate pool. Across three independent enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA (Reactome + SMPDB + KEGG + WikiPathways), mummichog m/z-network activity, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA — the KEGG 'Methionine Metabolism' map (hsa00670) emerges as the top cross-paradigm winner (MetaboAnalystR rank 1, p=3.36e-07; RaMP rank 4, FDR 1.19e-13; mummichog rank 2, p=0.0155), with 5 input metabolites — L-methionine (KEGG:C00073), S-adenosylmethionine (KEGG:C00019), homocysteine (KEGG:C00155), choline (KEGG:C00114), and adenosine (KEGG:C00212) — hitting the pathway. The driver metabolites define the canonical cycle: L-methionine is the entry substrate converted by methionine adenosyltransferase to SAM, which donates its methyl group to methyltransferases and generates SAH that is hydrolyzed to adenosine and homocysteine; homocysteine is then either remethylated (requiring folate/betaine) or enters the transsulfuration branch. Choline feeds the betaine-dependent remethylation route. Cysteic acid (C00506) maps to the downstream cysteine-oxidation arm of transsulfuration, confirming full flux through the cycle. Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:map00260) ranks as a secondary consensus hit (RaMP rank 0, FDR 3.75e-19) via shared one-carbon donors (L-threonine, L-glutamic acid, choline), consistent with a broad perturbation of one-carbon metabolism affecting both methionine and glycine cycles simultaneously. final_react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolome is driven by a coordinated perturbation of methionine metabolism and its connected one-carbon/folate pool. Across three independent enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA (Reactome + SMPDB + KEGG + WikiPathways), mummichog m/z-network activity, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA — the KEGG 'Methionine Metabolism' map (hsa00670) emerges as the top cross-paradigm winner (MetaboAnalystR rank 1, p=3.36e-07; RaMP rank 4, FDR 1.19e-13; mummichog rank 2, p=0.0155), with 5 input metabolites — L-methionine (KEGG:C00073), S-adenosylmethionine (KEGG:C00019), homocysteine (KEGG:C00155), choline (KEGG:C00114), and adenosine (KEGG:C00212) — hitting the pathway. The driver metabolites define the canonical cycle: L-methionine is the entry substrate converted by methionine adenosyltransferase to SAM, which donates its methyl group to methyltransferases and generates SAH that is hydrolyzed to adenosine and homocysteine; homocysteine is then either remethylated (requiring folate/betaine) or enters the transsulfuration branch. Choline feeds the betaine-dependent remethylation route. Cysteic acid (C00506) maps to the downstream cysteine-oxidation arm of transsulfuration, confirming full flux through the cycle. Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:map00260) ranks as a secondary consensus hit (RaMP rank 0, FDR 3.75e-19) via shared one-carbon donors (L-threonine, L-glutamic acid, choline), consistent with a broad perturbation of one-carbon metabolism affecting both methionine and glycine cycles simultaneously. The lipid signals (15-HETE, 8-HPETE) point to secondary lipoxygenase activity on arachidonic acid, which does not reach significance in ORA and likely reflects inflammatory co-activation downstream of oxidative stress in the one-carbon pool.
